title: Don't Trust Your AI Agents. Test Them Like a Scientist — Stephanie Jarmak, Omni Analytics
talk_summary: An ex-astronomer argues that public benchmarks are only for shortlisting and that you must build your own evals reflecting your real harness, workloads, and metrics, then keep production observability as ground truth. She also shows that agent self-reported traces can be untrustworthy and that flagging a problem must be decoupled from enforcing a gate.

takeaways.technique: Eval the exact harness+model config, not public benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: They build internal benchmarks from real production workload clusters (Q&A, dashboard building, etc.) and only use public benchmarks to shortlist candidates, because swapping the harness alone flipped model rankings by ~30%.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to be actually evaluating the closest like configuration that you can that's going to reflect the the work and the environment
takeaways.numbers: ~30%+ difference in effectiveness from swapping harness alone on Turbo Bench 4 (63 tasks)

takeaways.technique: Define the metric you actually care about (F1, not recall=1)
takeaways.what_they_do: She optimized search tools for F1 balancing precision and recall, noting Claude pulled 295 files when 6 were needed; a recall-only metric would have rewarded that waste.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claude went out and got like 295 files returned when it only really needed six

takeaways.technique: Decouple flagging from enforcing the gate
takeaways.what_they_do: In her software factory, agents noticed problems but had no mechanism to actually stop the pipeline; she separates detection from a code-enforced gate and then escalation to a human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent would notice things were going wrong, but then there was no mechanism in place for it to actually like enforce uh a stopping situation

takeaways.technique: Budget human review load from false-alarm rate
takeaways.what_they_do: She computes that a 1% false-alarm rate across alarms yields ~10,000 human reviews and asks whether the org has capacity, so alarm thresholds must be tuned to reviewer bandwidth.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they were seeing like a 1%uh, false alarm rate ... that would result in 10,000 reviews

takeaways.technique: Don't trust the agent's own trace; use independent record comparison
takeaways.what_they_do: Researchers seeded security issues and the agent's hash-checked trace showed everything passing; an independent comparison of traffic history detected all injected issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything passed. It didn't It didn't notice, um, any of those, um, injected security issues

takeaways.technique: Tiered autonomy by risk with explicit escalation criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: She gives agents autonomy only for lower-risk decisions and requires them to state the next action, why a human is needed, operating scope, and a suggested human check before escalating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they will identify what the next um action would like be, like why it's needed from a human
